input.quote: 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
input.rationale: The Services licence in § 13.1 fails the fallback: it names Customer alone, expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them, is non-transferable, and is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — which is walk-away territory under this rule. The counterweights only partly help: § 13.2's perpetual, irrevocable licence covering Affiliates and contractors is limited to paid-up software and embedded Deliverables, and § 13.3 (transfer to an Affiliate or successor; revocation only for material uncured breach after notice and cure) contradicts § 13.1's at-will revocation rather than curing the Affiliate/contractor exclusion for the Services. Our redline conforms § 13.1 to the preferred position by extending use to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, tying revocation to the § 13.3 notice-and-cure standard, and adding successor transfer via the § 24 assignment right.

proposal.summary: Extend the Services licence to Affiliates and contractors and remove revocation at Vendor's discretion
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Services licence to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, and replaced revocation at Vendor's sole discretion with the notice-and-cure standard already agreed in Section 13.3, consistent with our licence-scope position. If helpful, we can accept Affiliate coverage on written notice as a fallback.

ops.oldText: Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
ops.newText: Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates, and contractors acting on Customer's behalf, a licence to use the Services, revocable or suspendable only as permitted by Section 13.3 and transferable to a successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24.
